quiz.question: What do objects use to organize their data, unlike arrays?
quiz.explanation: Objects use named key-value pairs (properties) to organize data, while arrays use numbered positions (indices).

quiz.question: Which of the following is a valid TypeScript object?
quiz.explanation: Objects are defined with curly braces {} containing key-value pairs separated by commas.

quiz.question: What types of values can properties in a single object hold?

answers.answer: Different types can be mixed in one object
All properties must be the same type

quiz.explanation: An object can mix different types in one value. In the lesson example, the person object has a string (name), a number (age), and a boolean (active).
